properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: THE core cryptographic asset: secp256k1 ECDSA is the blockchain's signature scheme — every transaction output, every block, every key in this system. Implementation is the vendored libsecp256k1 (src/secp256k1/**: ecdsa, eckey, ecmult, recovery, multiset modules), consumed by the node through src/key.cpp (secp256k1_ecdsa_sign / sign_recoverable with RFC6979 nonces), src/pubkey.cpp (verify), src/bitcoin-tx.cpp (Secp256k1Init), and mirrored by the Python test framework's ctypes OpenSSL bindings. 30

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-scaffolding randomness, no security context despite the rule name: 72 sites are (a) Python's Mersenne-Twister random module in functional tests and test-vector generators (contrib/testgen, qa/rpc-tests) choosing tx amounts, OP_RETURN payloads and branch counts; (b) the C++ insecure_rand() fast PRNG in unit tests (coins_tests, sighash_tests, merkle_tests, pmt_tests, skiplist_tests, crypto_tests) for coverage-driven simulation. No production call site — production randomness lives in src/rand

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Digest comparisons via ==/!=, uniformly on PUBLIC blockchain data: block-hash equality checks in main.cpp genesis handling, checkpoints.cpp, miner.cpp asserts, mempool outpoint iteration (txmempool.cpp), inflightindex.cpp bookkeeping, blocksender.cpp, plus uint256 operator== in primitives/transaction.h; test-side are Python asserts on block hashes and BOOST_CHECKs against expected vectors in crypto_tests.cpp. None guards a secret or an authentication decision — no MAC comparison, no timing-obser

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenSSL ECDSA over secp256k1, used in three roles: (1) qa/rpc-tests/test_framework/key.py drives OpenSSL EC_KEY_new_by_curve_name/ECDSA_sign through ctypes so functional tests can sign transactions — the framework's signing workhorse; (2) src/secp256k1/src/bench_verify.c and (3) tests.c cross-check the vendored secp256k1 implementation against OpenSSL's ECDSA. No production ECDSA call site outside secp256k1 itself — the node signs via the vendored library (see secp256k1 object). Quantum-vulnerab

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH over secp256k1, vendored as a module of the bundled libsecp256k1 (src/secp256k1/src/modules/ecdh). CI matrix (.travis.yml) builds it for several configurations (ECDH=yes, plus one ECDH=no baseline) and bench_ecdh.c measures it. Not wired into the node's protocol — Bitcoin's P2P layer does no key agreement — so this is capability in the shipped library, exercised by builds and benchmarks only. Observable here; removal/retention is a build-flag decision. ECDH is Shor-relevant only if some con

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unit tests for the production HMAC implementations CHMAC_SHA256 (src/crypto/hmac_sha256.cpp) and CHMAC_SHA512 (src/crypto/hmac_sha512.cpp), running RFC 4231 vectors. The primitives themselves are load-bearing: HMAC-SHA512 is BIP32 hierarchical key derivation, HMAC-SHA256 was used for the alert CMF. Symmetric primitives — Grover margin only, no Shor exposure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Genuine CSPRNG use on both files: os.urandom() (CPython's OS-entropy CSPRNG) generates random byte payloads for the base58 test-vector generator, and OpenSSL RAND_bytes backs Bitcoin Core's own random layer (src/random.cpp GetRandBytes). Not quantum-relevant (an RNG is not Shor-vulnerable) and not a weak-PRNG finding — these are the strong, correct choices — but they belong in the crypto inventory as the PRNG that keys all first-party key material. Changeable here.
